details: Escalating US-Iran tensions, including recent military actions and impacts on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, are significantly affecting global energy markets. This has led to a rise in crude oil prices and a broader risk-off sentiment in financial markets, causing investors to move away from volatile assets. The IMF has noted that Saudi Arabia's economic recovery is contingent on the normalization of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Middle East Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher, Sparking Risk-Off Mood

details: Bitcoin experienced a significant price drop, trading near $66,800, after a difficult start to June. This decline is attributed to sustained spot Bitcoin ETF outflows, which saw $519 million exit on June 2 alone, extending a twelve-day negative streak to over $3.2 billion. Geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and a rotation of institutional capital into AI-related equities are also cited as key factors.
title: Bitcoin Plunges Amid Heavy ETF Outflows and Geopolitical Fears

details: Eurozone flash inflation rose to 3.2% in May, surpassing April's figures and economists' expectations. Core inflation also climbed to 2.5%, indicating broader price pressures. These figures reinforce strong expectations for a 25 basis point interest rate hike by the European Central Bank at its upcoming June 11th meeting.
title: Eurozone Inflation Accelerates to 3.2%, ECB Rate Hike Imminent

details: Strong enthusiasm for Artificial Intelligence (AI) continues to drive gains in US, European, and Asian equity markets, particularly in semiconductor and software sectors. This AI-led rally is contributing to a rotation of institutional capital away from digital assets, as investors seek higher volatility and growth prospects in AI-linked equities. Upcoming IPOs like OpenAI and SpaceX are further diverting speculative interest.
title: AI Boom Draws Capital Away from Crypto Markets

details: The International Monetary Fund completed its 2026 Article IV Mission to Saudi Arabia, noting the economy's resilience despite ongoing Middle East conflicts. However, the IMF's forecast of approximately 2% GDP growth for 2026 is explicitly contingent on the normalization of maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring significant geopolitical downside risks.
title: IMF: Saudi Economy Resilient, but Strait of Hormuz Key to Recovery

details: Piero Cipollone, Member of the Executive Board of the European Central Bank, provided an update on the digital euro project. He highlighted agreements with European standard-setting bodies and preparations for a piloting exercise in the second half of 2027. The project aims to complement cash, ensuring monetary sovereignty and offering diverse payment options.
title: ECB Progresses Digital Euro, Pilot Scheduled for Late 2027

details: A recent survey conducted for the American Bankers Association revealed that a significant majority of consumers (57% vs. 19%) support prohibiting crypto companies from offering interest-like rewards for holding stablecoins. This sentiment comes as the U.S. Senate prepares to consider the Clarity Act, aimed at regulating digital assets, with proponents arguing such a ban would protect local bank deposits and lending.
title: Americans Back Ban on Stablecoin Yields Amid Regulatory Debate
